jobs.description:
Context & Environment

Join the Field Operations teams of TotalEnergies in Denmark and contribute to improving the operational performance and safety of offshore activities.

Within the Field Operations Support and Operational Safety departments, you will contribute to the development of management tools, budget monitoring, preparation of regulatory audits and improvement of internal processes.

Please check your eligibility for the VIE program and the country-specific requirements on the following website: https://mon-vie-via.businessfrance.fr/qu-est-ce-que-le-volontariat-international

Please apply in English.

Accommodation will be provided by the affiliate.

Activities

You will work with two distinct teams, Operations Support and Operational Safety. Beyond the responsibilities specific to each activity, you will participate in cross-functional projects related to continuous improvement, reporting and ways-of-working transformation, providing you with a broader understanding of Field Operations activities.

Your main responsibilities:

• Develop and improve automated reporting tools for operational teams.

• Build and enhance Power BI dashboards.

• Produce performance indicators and data analyses.

• Participate in budget monitoring and cost data consolidation.

• Update organisational data and organisational charts.

• Prepare regulatory audits and coordinate associated actions.

• Contribute to HSE topic monitoring and root cause analyses.

• Prepare presentations and materials for management.

• Identify improvement opportunities and propose innovative solutions.

You hold at least a Master's degree (BAC+5) from an engineering school or equivalent, with a specialisation in process engineering, chemical engineering, HSE or risk management.

You have initial experience (internship, apprenticeship or professional experience) involving data analysis, cost monitoring, reporting or project management.

Experience in HSE topics, audits or risk management within the industrial or energy sector would be an asset.

Experience in developing digital tools is appreciated.

You are proficient in Microsoft Office tools, particularly:

• Excel

• PowerPoint

• Power BI (for data visualisation)

A minimum C1 level in English is required. A minimum B2 level in French is also required.

jobs.occupation: Expert, Business Area Manager Ecotoxicology and Environment
jobs.description:
Could your expertise in ecotoxicology help shape better environmental decisions—and unlock new opportunities for science-led advisory services?

At DHI, you’ll connect ecotoxicology, environmental science and water modelling to help clients tackle complex challenges in aquatic environments. Join our international Environment & Toxicology team to broaden your impact while helping grow our environmental advisory business.

Responsibilities and Challenges

We are looking for a senior colleague with expertise in ecotoxicology and environmental science with insights and interests in developing our advisory solutions and business.

As a member of DHI’s international Environment & Toxicology team, you will help clients address complex challenges related to chemicals, ecotoxicology and the aquatic environment. You will work closely with clients and colleagues across disciplines to develop practical, science-based solutions that protect human health and the environment.

The main responsibilities are to:

• Deliver expert advisory within the area of regulatory and scientific aspects of eco-toxicology, environmental exposure- and risk assessment, management of chemicals and/or environmental hazardous substances in water environments, and other client projects.

• Lead business development within advisory area of environment and eco-toxicology, enabling and bringing to life the strategy to build on the markets for advisory on environmental exposure- and risk assessment, management of chemicals and/or environmental hazardous substances (incl. micropollutants) in water environments.

• Plan and execute of internal and external activities of knowledge distribution (i.e. network meetings, conferences or courses) as well as business development activities.

• Serve as project manager in own projects, as well as deliver as project participant in projects within the portfolio.

• Perform quality assurance and mentor young colleagues, ensuring high scientific level of solutions.

• Establish and maintain good practices for international collaboration in E&T.

What We're Looking For

Required education, experience and capabilities

• A relevant university degree in ecotoxicology, environmental chemistry, environmental science, biology, chemistry, chemical engineering, water or environmental engineering, or a closely related discipline. A PhD or other advanced qualification is an advantage.

• At least 7 years of relevant professional experience in ecotoxicology, environmental chemistry, environmental risk assessment, chemicals in the environment or a closely related advisory field.

• A strong professional track record gained in consultancy, industry, public authority, research organization, or a comparable environment.

• Demonstrated experience assessing chemicals or environmentally hazardous substances in aquatic or water-related environments.

• Experience leading technically complex projects, including responsibility for scope, quality, budget, schedule and stakeholder management.

• A proven ability to originate or develop business, build client relationships and contribute to successful proposals or tenders.

• A good understanding of relevant environmental regulation, market developments and the needs of industry and public-sector clients.

• Experience working in an international or multidisciplinary setting.

• Proficient in English (professional level)

Additional experience and strengths, which will contribute to success in this role:

• Experience with establishing environmental quality standards and predicted no-effect concentrations, and/or assessing chemicals in wastewater or other water environments

• Knowledge of the EU Water Framework Directive, Urban Waste Water Treatment Directive, Drinking Water Directive or related national requirements.

• Experience with environmental fate, transport or exposure modelling

• Collaboration with authorities, utilities, industrial clients, industry associations, research programmes or international consortia.

• Experience developing services or markets across Denmark and the wider European region.

• Serving as the technical lead and/or mentor for colleagues in a team.

Skills and competences

The successful candidate combines scientific credibility with commercial awareness and a genuine interest in understanding client needs. We are looking for a person who can translate complex scientific and regulatory matters into clear advice and practical solutions.

You are:

• Scientifically strong, with the ability to provide authoritative advice within your field.

• Client-oriented and commercially aware, with the confidence to initiate conversations, develop opportunities and build lasting professional relationships.

• An effective project leader, able to maintain direction and quality across technically complex assignments.

• A clear communicator, capable of engaging scientific experts, decision-makers, authorities and other stakeholders.

• Collaborative and internationally oriented, with an interest in working across disciplines, markets and organisational boundaries.

• Proactive and accountable, taking ownership and exercising sound professional judgement.

• Generous with your expertise, contributing to knowledge sharing, mentoring and the professional development of colleagues.

Why join DHI?

To work at DHI means being part of an organisation that is the global leader in solving the world’s toughest challenges in water, environment and sustainability.

In this position we offer to you the opportunity to join a strong company with dedicated colleagues to:

• Shape and grow DHI’s ecotoxicology and environmental advisory business.

• Work at the intersection of chemicals, water environments, environmental regulation and data-driven decision-making.

• Collaborate with ecotoxicologists, environmental scientists, toxicologists, water specialists and modellers across an international organisation.

• Lead meaningful assignments for industry, authorities, utilities and partners.

• Take on a visible expert role with opportunities to influence strategy, develop clients, lead projects and mentor colleagues.

DHI is a global and independent company dedicated to working on challenges within the fields of water and environment and sustainability. Within these fields, we provide a wide range of advisory, digital advisory, research and water governance services as well as providing leading edge MIKE technologies and products to the market. At DHI, we are constantly looking for passionate and talented people who are eager to join our team.

By joining DHI, you will not only become part of a dynamic and collaborative global team of experts; you will be empowered to innovate, engage and grow in your area of expertise. DHI is committed to disseminate our knowledge effectively and across our worldwide network of offices.

Location & Mobility

• The role location is at DHI office, Hørsholm, Denmark

Travelling must be expected in the role to enable collaboration with clients and/or inside DHI. Travelling rules as included in employment contract

How to apply

• Please submit your application including CV via the relevant job posting on DHI’s website: http://www.dhigroup.com/careers

• Deadline for application is 26th November 2026.

• For further information please contact Yong Quan Lim, Talent Acquisition Specialist by by email liyq@dhigroup.com / Lise Lyck, Senior manager, Environment & Toxicology by email lly@dhigroup.com.

Would you like to contribute to ensuring high-quality pharmaceutical production while helping us simplify and improve the way we work? Do you have a strong quality mindset, excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to adapt in a changing environment?

We are looking for an experienced QA professional who combines strong quality awareness with curiosity and an improvement mindset. Every day we seek the solutions that defeat serious chronic diseases. To do this, we approach our work with determination, constant curiosity and a commitment to finding better ways forward. For over 100 years, this dedication has driven us to build a company focused on lasting change for long-term health. One where diverse thinking, shared purpose and mutual respect come together to create extraordinary results. When you join us, you're not just starting a job – you're becoming part of a story that spans generations.

**💰 🇩🇰 up to 46,000 DKK gross/month (depending on seniority level)

**Intro

Monta powers the EV charging ecosystem. With 300,000+ monthly users and millions of charge sessions every month, our platform accelerates the electrification of mobility.

This is a fast-moving place. The problems are hard, the pace is quick, and the bar is high. If you like real ownership, figuring things out, and seeing the direct impact of your work, you’ll do well with us.

AI is built into how we work. It helps us ship faster, make better decisions, and stay lean. Everyone at Monta is expected to use AI tools thoughtfully - and to find smart ways to use them to move the work forward.

Our principles keep us grounded: Build Together & Finish, Sweat the Details, Customer First, and Aim for the Moon.

The best part of Monta is the people - sharp, ambitious, and good to be around. You’ll be challenged, supported, and trusted to deliver.

We’re looking for a Jun/Mid Level Engineer who’s ready to roll up their sleeves, take ownership, and build with us - through the grind and the wins.

This Is What You Will Achieve

• Owned an OCPP hardening project - chased down a recurring class of vendor quirks (malformed messages, connection drops, the long tail of hardware oddities), shipped the fix, and measurably cut failed sessions or disconnections for that device family.

• Helped shift the team from reacting to incidents to preventing them, through alerting and observability work that catches problems earlier.

• Made real progress on OCPP 1.6, OCPP 2.0.1, and OCPI standards work that other services and front-ends across Monta now rely on.

What You Will Do

• Build and maintain backend services in NetOps' OCPP and charge point domain - protocol handling, message processing, device state, integrations with hardware vendors.

• Debug things that only break in the field. A charge point in Belgium disconnects every 40 minutes - you'll read the OCPP traffic, reproduce it against our emulator, find the cause, and fix it.

• Improve observability and alerting. Add the metrics, dashboards, and alerts that mean the next person doesn't have to guess.

• Take part in on-call once you're ramped up, with a team that treats a rough night as a reason to fix the system, not a rite of passage.

• Automate manual work away - a meaningful part of NetOps' job is removing the human steps that don't scale as our network grows.

• Collaborate across Product, Support, and the operations teams who live with the consequences of what we ship. You won't work in a silo.

**A Brief Overview Of Our Tech Stack

**

• Kotlin services (JVM), with Java where it already lives

• PHP/Laravel monolith - parts of our charge point domain still run here

• OCPP 1.6 / 2.0.1 and OCPI protocol handling

• Event-driven work with Kafka where message volume calls for it

• Observability via Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenSearch/Kibana

• AWS + Kubernetes, with Terraform for infrastructure

What We’re Looking For

• 1–4 years of backend engineering experience, or a strong junior track record with real production exposure. You write clean, readable code and finish what you start.

• Comfortable in a JVM language - Kotlin preferred, Java fine, and we'll help you get there from another stack if the fundamentals are strong. Willingness to touch PHP in our legacy monolith when the work calls for it.

• You enjoy debugging, genuinely - logs, traces, packet-level detail, weird one-off reports from a single customer.

• A sense of ownership - you follow your work into production, watch it, and flag problems early rather than waiting to be asked.

• Nice to have: curiosity about the physical world (our systems talk to metal boxes with electricity in them); clear communication - you can explain what broke and why to someone who isn't an engineer; advanced, deliberate use of AI tools in your daily engineering workflow.

• Bonus points for: exposure to OCPP, OCPI, EV charging, or the EV industry as a driver or enthusiast; IoT, embedded, or telemetry systems where devices in the field misbehave; event-driven architectures (Kafka) or high-volume message processing; reliability/monitoring/on-call experience (Prometheus, Grafana, SLOs); Kubernetes, Terraform, or infrastructure-as-code exposure.

**If the mission excites you but your experience isn’t a perfect 1:1 match, apply anyway - we care about potential, not perfection.

**AI Competency

• You’ll be expected to work with AI-powered tools. Some we use:

• GitHub Copilot / Claude Code

• ChatGPT / Gemini / Claude

• Notion AI (docs, knowledge, meeting notes)

• Analytics & ML: Langfuse, PyTorch, Mastra

• AI-enhanced testing & monitoring (e.g., generative QA, Grafana ML)

• We don’t expect mastery of all - but we expect comfort learning, experimenting, and adopting AI responsibly.

Why Monta

• Impact, not easy mode - your work matters, and you’ll feel it every day.

• Ownership from day one - we don’t micromanage, we expect you to deliver.

• The grind is real - priorities shift, and flexibility is sometimes needed to get things across the finish line. But so are the rewards: impact, growth, and a team that has your back.

• The people are extraordinary - talented, driven, and fun to work with. You’ll be challenged, supported, and inspired in equal measure.

What We Offer

• A yearly education budget and extra days off to use it.

• A friendly and social company culture with movie nights, Friday bars, pub crawls, and more.

• Free lunch every day.

• Pension & health coverage to keep you secure for today and tomorrow.

• Paid parental leave to support life's big moments.

• Warrants program - be part of our growth story.

• Flexible working hours; as long as you're at key meetings and delivering great work, we trust you to manage your schedule.

Please send us your application in English.

To succeed in this position, your spoken and written English skills need to be proficient. Since Monta is a globally active company, you'll be communicating often and regularly with our co-workers and partners around the world, making your professional English knowledge essential.

Would you like to play a key role in ensuring a smooth and professional experience for our clients while working at the intersection of energy, data, systems and operations?

The team is responsible for the operational client journey after a contract has been signed. This includes onboarding and offboarding assets, managing master data, coordinating operational processes, and ensuring that the necessary systems, registrations, and stakeholders are aligned.

The position is full-time, fixed-term maternity cover expected to run from January through December 2027.

• Collect, import and quality-assure metering data and asset master data. Ensure that internal systems are configured correctly and that the required registrations are completed.

• Coordinate supplier switching and related market processes.

• Follow up with internal and external stakeholders to ensure that onboarding activities are completed on time.

Daily operations and client coordination

• Identify missing information, clarify uncertainties, and make sure issues are followed through to completion.

• Maintain accurate documentation and ensure that relevant information is available to the teams that depend on it.

• Contribute to a reliable and professional day-to-day experience for our clients.

Cross-functional responsibility and improvements

• Collaborate closely with colleagues in Sales, Trading, Settlement, IT, and other operational teams.

• Coordinate dependencies across teams and ensure clear ownership of outstanding tasks.

• Identify opportunities to simplify, standardise, and automate manual processes.

• Contribute to the further development of our master-data platform and operational tools.

• Explore how automation and AI can improve quality, efficiency, and scalability in the team’s work.

We need a colleague who enjoys working with structure, data and systems, and who takes responsibility for getting processes safely across the line. If you like working in detail, keeping track of many dependencies and at the same time being curious about smarter solutions, you will fit in perfectly here with us.

Anders Borup

Head of Energy Asset Integration & Operations

Do you want to help shape how a large IT company measures, manages and documents its information security? Are you motivated by turning data, risk and regulation into practical decisions? If so, you may be our next colleague in the newly established GRC team in Netcompany's Group CISO Office.

Responsibilities and technologies

As a member of the GRC team, you will help ensure that Netcompany has an accurate, data-driven view of the effectiveness of its security controls and its level of compliance. The team takes a pragmatic and technically grounded approach to governance, risk and compliance, and works closely with the Application Security team, the Operations organisation, Internal IT and other business functions across the group.

The GRC team is a small team of colleagues with complementary profiles. We do not expect any one candidate to cover every area described below. Instead, we are looking for broad profiles with solid experience across several of these areas and the motivation to develop within the rest.

Your responsibilites will typically include:

• Developing and maintaining risk scenarios, assessing the effectiveness of mitigating controls against the scenarios, and conducting risk assessments to support business decisions

• Establishing automated measurements and KPIs that provide insight into the implementation and effectiveness of security controls across the business

• Interpreting regulatory and contractual security requirements and translating these into Netcompany's security baselines and standard methodologies

• Planning and executing security awareness activities, including phishing simulations, targeted micro-learning, and onboarding/yearly awareness training

Department of Mathematical Sciences, Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen

  The Department of Mathematical Sciences at the University of Copenhagen is seeking top early-career researchers for a number of attractive one- to three-year postdoctoral positions.

  The Department of Mathematical Sciences has strong research groups in many areas of applied mathematics, and has an active postdoc and visitors' program. Applicants in all areas of mathematics covered by the research groups of the department will be considered.

  There will be postdoc stipends in the following specific areas:

   	
• Insurance mathematics, optimization and operations research, mathematical finance, econometrics and financial economics, and applied probability theory, covered by the Section for Insurance and Economics. 	
• Probability theory, mathematical statistics and applied statistics, covered by the Section for Statistics and Probability Theory.   In particular, the following specific positions are open:

   	
• Variational analysis in the Wasserstein space of stochastic processes (contact Johannes Wiesel wiesel@math.ku.dk) 	
• Causal modelling and related questions in reliable machine learning (contact Sebastian Weichwald, https://sweichwald.de/#research-with-us). Applicants are encouraged to describe a concrete research direction, what they bring to it, and why it fits the group’s work. 	
• Causal Inference and Interpretability in Complex Models (contact Nikolaj Thams, thams@math.ku.dk ) 	
• Optimization under decision-dependent uncertainty (contact Giovanni Pantuso, gp@math.ku.dk)    

  The postdoc’s duties will include research within mathematics as well as teaching. The teaching load is typically two half-semester courses per year, of which one usually is as a teaching assistant. The post may also include performance of other project-specific duties.

  The positions are open with starting date in 2027, ordinarily September 1st or as soon as possible thereafter. The salary is very competitive and researchers from outside Denmark may qualify for a reduced tax rate (see terms below).

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Further information on the Department is linked at https://www.math.ku.dk/ . Inquiries about the position can be made to the Head of Department Mogens Steffensen, mogens@math.ku.dk.

   

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include 

   	
• Curriculum vitae: 1-3 pages, including list of publications. 	
• Cover letter: Substantiate your qualification for the postdoc position and your motivations. 	
• Diplomas: Master and PhD degree or equivalent. If you do not yet have a PhD diploma, please just upload a PDF stating your (expected) PhD date. 	
• Research plan: Description of current and future research plans (1-3 pages). 	
• Separate reprints of 3 particularly relevant papers (not mandatory)    

  The deadline for applications is 15th of November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. We expect to send invitations for interviews in December 2026 or January 2027. The interviews will typically take place in January and February of 2026, and our search is expected to be concluded around April 2027.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

We are looking for a motivated Fundraising & Project Development Intern to help Pangaea Youth Network develop new projects and secure funding for our local and international activities. You will have the opportunity to work on real funding applications and contribute directly to the growth and development of a youth NGO.

LocationHorsensHorsens, Denmark/Hybrid

DurationFlexible, adjustable

TopicFundraising, Grant Writing, Project Development & NGO Management

TypeInternship

Description

Position Overview:

This is a hands-on internship where you will work closely with our management and project team to identify funding opportunities, develop fundraising strategies, create new project ideas, and prepare grant applications.

You will help turn ideas into real projects by researching funding programmes, developing project concepts, planning activities, preparing budgets, and writing applications for funding.

Our main focus is on Erasmus+ projects, Danish foundations, municipal funding opportunities, and international programmes supporting youth work, education, inclusion, community development, sustainability, and international cooperation.

Responsibilities:

• 
Fundraising Strategy: Research and develop fundraising strategies for PYN, identify potential funding sources, analyse funding requirements, and help create a long-term fundraising plan for the organisation.

• 
Funding Research: Identify relevant grants and funding opportunities from Erasmus+, Danish foundations, municipalities, EU programmes, and international funding organisations. Monitor application deadlines, eligibility requirements, funding priorities, and available budgets.

• 
Project Development: Help develop new local and international project ideas based on PYN’s mission, community needs, and funding opportunities. Contribute to defining project objectives, target groups, activities, expected results, and long-term impact.

• 
Grant Writing: Prepare and write funding applications, including project descriptions, needs analysis, objectives, activities, methodology, expected outcomes, sustainability plans, and dissemination strategies.

• 
Project Budgets: Support the preparation of project budgets, financial plans, funding requests, and cost estimates in cooperation with the management and accounting team.

• 
Partnership Development: Research potential local and international project partners, foundations, sponsors, and organisations. Support communication with stakeholders and help develop partnerships for future funding applications.

• 
Project Planning: Help create project timelines, work plans, activity schedules, responsibilities, and implementation strategies for proposed projects.

• 
Funding Database: Maintain an organised overview of funding opportunities, application deadlines, eligibility criteria, application progress, submitted proposals, and funding results.

• 
Organisational Development: Contribute ideas for improving PYN’s financial sustainability, expanding its activities, and developing new services or initiatives that could attract additional funding.

Skills & Qualifications:

We are looking for someone who is interested in fundraising, project management, international cooperation, and NGO development. And has:

• 
Good written English (preferably B2 or higher)

• 
Strong research and analytical skills

• 
Good organisational skills

• 
Attention to details

• 
Creativity

• 
The ability to work independently

You should feel comfortable using Google Docs, Google Sheets, or similar digital tools and be interested in developing and writing structured project proposals.

Nice to have:

Previous experience with Erasmus+, grant writing, fundraising, project management, budgeting, research, or NGO work. Familiarity with EU funding programmes, Danish foundations, or project application processes is an advantage but not required.

Personal qualities:

We appreciate people who are proactive, curious, responsible, detail-oriented, and motivated to learn. You should enjoy developing ideas, researching opportunities, solving problems, and turning concepts into practical project proposals.

Relevant study backgrounds:

Project Management, International Relations, Business Administration, Economics, Public Administration, Political Science, Social Sciences, European Studies, Nonprofit Management, or related fields. Students from other backgrounds are also welcome to apply.

Working Style & Environment:

Our office and youth space are located in Student Village Kamtjatka, in the city centre of Horsens, Denmark.

A hybrid working setup is possible, but we prefer interns who can be present on-site for teamwork, project development meetings, and organisational activities.

Typical office hours are around 9:00:00–16:30, Monday–Friday, with the remaining working hours arranged according to the internship agreement and team needs.

You will join a small, international team working across project management, fundraising, marketing, community events, accounting, web development, and youth work.

You will work closely with PYN’s management and receive guidance on project development, funding research, and grant writing. At the same time, you will have opportunities to take responsibility for your own research, project concepts, and application drafts.

What You Gain:

• 
Practical Fundraising Experience: Learn how NGOs identify funding opportunities, approach funders, develop fundraising strategies, and prepare grant applications.

• 
Real Project Development Experience: Participate in developing actual local and international projects, from the initial idea to a complete funding application.

• 
Erasmus+ Knowledge: Gain practical insight into European funding programmes, international partnerships, project planning, grant writing, and the management of EU-funded initiatives.

• 
Professional Development: Improve your research, analytical thinking, project design, budgeting, strategic planning, professional writing, and stakeholder communication skills.

• 
International Working Environment: Become part of a supportive international community and collaborate with young people, interns, volunteers, and partners from different countries.

• 
Networking Opportunities: Build connections with NGOs, foundations, international organisations, local stakeholders, and potential project partners.

• 
Erasmus+ Mobility Opportunities: Depending on your availability, eligibility, and participant profile, you may have opportunities to join Erasmus+ youth exchanges and training courses (typically 5–10 days), where travel, food, and accommodation are covered by EU funds.

• 
Meaningful Impact: Contribute to securing resources that help PYN organise free community activities, international learning opportunities, youth projects, and initiatives that benefit young people.

Note:

This is an unpaid internship. Pangaea Youth Network does not provide monetary compensation or financial support.

We offer practical professional experience, supervision, an international working environment, networking opportunities, access to relevant Erasmus+ activities, and opportunities to contribute to real projects with a positive social impact.
